message: Ballotpedia uses 'email', not 'e-mail'.
suggestion: email

message: Ballotpedia uses 'bipartisan', not 'bi-partisan'.
suggestion: bipartisan

message: Ballotpedia uses 'healthcare' as one word in narrative text.
suggestion: healthcare

message: Ballotpedia prefers 'judgment'.
suggestion: judgment

message: Use 'midterm election', not 'mid-term election'.
suggestion: midterm election

message: Write 'noncitizen' without a hyphen.
suggestion: noncitizen

message: Write 'nonpartisan' as one word.
suggestion: nonpartisan

message: Write 'nonprofit' as one word.
suggestion: nonprofit

message: Ballotpedia uses 'toward', not 'towards'.
suggestion: toward

message: Write 'runoff' as one word.
suggestion: runoff

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Comprised of, composed of
message: Ballotpedia recommends 'composed of', 'made up of', or a correct 'comprises' construction rather than 'comprised of'.
suggestion: Use 'composed of', 'made up of', or '[whole] comprises [parts]'.

message: Ballotpedia prefers 'advisor', but an official title may retain its official spelling.
suggestion: Use 'advisor' unless reproducing an official title.

message: Use the % sign with a numeral, with no space.
suggestion: Replace 'N percent' with 'N%'.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Dates, basic format
message: Do not use ordinal suffixes with dates.
suggestion: Use 'Month D, Year' rather than 'Month Dth, Year'.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Today, tomorrow, tonight; BP News best practices
message: Ballotpedia prefers specific dates to relative time markers because content may be read later.
suggestion: Replace the relative time marker with the specific date when known.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Quotations, Scare quotes
message: The guide says never to use 'so-called'; it often functions as a scare-quote signal.
suggestion: State the term neutrally, attribute it, or describe the underlying concept.

message: When reporting a death, Ballotpedia uses direct phrasing with 'died' rather than euphemisms.
suggestion: Use 'NAME died on DATE' when reporting the death.

message: Do not use 'public servant' to describe an individual; use the specific role category or title.
suggestion: Use 'elected official', 'appointed official', 'government employee', or the specific title.

message: Use 'same-sex marriage', not 'gay marriage', in Ballotpedia's own voice.
suggestion: same-sex marriage

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Left-wing, leftist, far-left
message: Ballotpedia says not to use these labels to describe a person's political ideology; describe affiliation, voting history, and issue stances instead.
suggestion: Replace the label with specific, sourced political affiliation or issue-position information.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Right-wing, rightist, far-right
message: Ballotpedia says not to use these labels to describe a person's political ideology; describe affiliation, voting history, and issue stances instead.
suggestion: Replace the label with specific, sourced political affiliation or issue-position information.

message: The guide says to avoid BIPOC and be specific about the racial and ethnic backgrounds being discussed.
suggestion: Use the specific racial/ethnic groups relevant to the sentence.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Person/people of color
message: The guide says to avoid this umbrella term and be specific about racial and ethnic backgrounds.
suggestion: Name the specific racial/ethnic groups or use a contextually supported alternative.

message: The guide treats Latinx and Latine as speech-tribe terms and directs writers to use its preferred Latino/Latina terminology or greater specificity.
suggestion: Use the Ballotpedia-preferred term appropriate to the person's identity/context, or be more specific.

message: The guide says to avoid 'mixed-race'; use biracial/multiracial when relevant and be specific when possible.
suggestion: Use 'biracial', 'multiracial', or specific heritage information as appropriate.

message: The guide says not to use these terms when describing disability.
suggestion: Use 'disabled people' or 'people with disabilities' as appropriate, following known preference when possible.

message: The guide identifies this immigration terminology as speech-tribe language in Ballotpedia's own voice.
suggestion: Use the guide's specific descriptive phrasing for the person's legal-residency context.

message: The guide lists 'migrant' among terms to avoid in the specified immigration-policy context; the word can have other meanings, so verify context.
suggestion: If describing people residing in the U.S. without legal permission, use the guide's specific descriptive phrasing.

message: The guide treats several common abortion-debate terms as speech-tribe or disfavored shorthand; source attribution and greater specificity may be required.
suggestion: Describe the specific policy position or use the guide's neutral alternatives; retain/attribute source terminology when the guide permits it.

message: The guide says these terms can function as speech-tribe shorthand; specify what the phrase means in the relevant policy context.
suggestion: Name the actual policy/service being discussed, such as contraception or abortion, when supported by the source.

pattern: \b(assault rifles?|assault weapons?|gun control|gun rights|constitutional carry|Second Amendment rights)\b
message: The guide identifies these firearms-policy phrases as speech-tribe or disfavored shorthand, subject to quotation/legal-term context.
suggestion: Describe the specific firearm policy or legal requirement; quote legal/source terminology when necessary.

message: The guide treats 'fake news' as speech-tribe terminology unless it appears in a quotation.
suggestion: Describe the alleged inaccuracy or misinformation specifically, or attribute the phrase to its source.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Clean energy, green energy
message: The guide prefers specific energy sources and says to avoid or attribute these broad terms unless they are part of a formal name.
suggestion: Specify wind, solar, hydropower, or the actual energy source/policy when supported.

message: The guide generally avoids this speech-tribe term outside quotations or formal names and prefers specific policy descriptions.
suggestion: Describe the policy or attribute the phrase to its source.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Greenhouse gases, emissions
message: The guide says to avoid these terms unless quoted or attributed and to specify the gas/emissions when possible.
suggestion: Specify carbon dioxide, methane, or the relevant emissions/policy when supported.

message: The guide treats 'gender-affirming care' as a speech-tribe term outside direct quotations.
suggestion: Use the guide's descriptive phrasing for social, psychological, and medical services for transgender individuals, adjusted to the actual services at issue.

message: The guide identifies these terms as speech-tribe/disfavored terminology in Ballotpedia's own voice.
suggestion: Use the guide's transgender terminology appropriate to the person and context.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Transgender, sports participation
message: For transgender sports coverage, the guide prefers 'sex' and says to quote 'biological sex' when it is the original legal language.
suggestion: Use 'sex' in Ballotpedia's own voice in the covered context; quote the legal wording when needed.

pattern: \b(sex assigned at birth|sex observed at birth)\b
message: The guide treats these phrases as speech-tribe terms and prefers 'sex' in Ballotpedia's own voice.
suggestion: Use 'sex' unless direct quotation or source-specific context requires otherwise.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Transgender; Transgender, sports participation
message: The guide cautions against partisan framing such as anti-trans legislation or describing sports eligibility rules as a ban on transgender athletes.
suggestion: Describe the legislation's operative requirements in neutral, specific terms.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Sexual commerce and exploitation
message: The guide treats 'sex work' as ideologically loaded language in Ballotpedia's own voice.
suggestion: Use the specific applicable term, such as commercial sexual solicitation, prostitution, or sex trafficking, based on the facts.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Public assistance programs
message: The guide says to be specific about the public-assistance program and not to use 'welfare' or 'food stamps'.
suggestion: Name the specific program, such as SNAP, Medicaid, or the relevant benefit program.

message: The guide prefers 'satellite spending' for the defined category and says not to use 'outside spending' or 'dark money' in Ballotpedia's own voice.
suggestion: Use 'satellite spending' if the spending fits the guide's definition.

pattern: \b(euthanasia|physician-assisted suicide|right to die|medically assisted suicide|death with dignity)\b
message: The guide says not to use these terms in Ballotpedia's own voice for the covered issue.
suggestion: Use 'physician-assisted death' or 'medical aid-in-dying' as appropriate.

message: Courtesy titles are reserved for direct quotations; avoid them in narrative text.
suggestion: Use the person's last name or appropriate political title in narrative text.

source: Ballotpedia Style Guide: Factive verbs; Ballotpedia bias taxonomy: Factive verbs
message: This verb can presuppose the truth of the attributed claim. It is acceptable for verifiable facts but may bias disputed opinions or narratives.
suggestion: If the claim is disputed/opinion, consider 'said', 'stated', or 'wrote'.

message: This is vague attribution. Identify the experts/source and provide evidence.
suggestion: Name the source(s) and attribute the claim specifically.

message: This construction can become a weasel claim when no study or source is identified.
suggestion: Name and cite the research if the sentence is not already clearly sourced.

source: Ballotpedia bias taxonomy: Editorializing / Loaded language / Inappropriate descriptors
message: This adverb may insert the writer's judgment rather than letting the sourced facts establish the point.
suggestion: Remove it or replace it with the specific evidence that makes the conclusion supportable.

message: Ballotpedia's bias guidance warns that evaluative adverbs can substitute interpretation for facts.
suggestion: Give the numerical margin or underlying fact when available.
